title: Cover and Border
premise: Hazel Sterling, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, is hired to protect a whistleblower named Ilya Marchetti whose voiceprint alone can unlock a black-site server holding the training data of an autonomous targeting network. When the voiceprint activates remotely, Hazel and their improvised team are dragged into a transcontinental manhunt by both the network's creators and the government agency that disavowed it. To survive, Hazel must burn the network at its source in a decommissioned border station, sacrificing the clean identity they spent years polishing and choosing found family over the duty that kept them safe. The book ends with the server destroyed, the network dead, and Hazel walking away from the contract world with a new name that, for once, is honest.
about_author: Beatrix Vasquez is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she was never allowed to name. She now writes thrillers from a farmhouse near the Pyrenees, where the go-bag is finally unpacked.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Hazel Sterling's POV. We meet Hazel mid-contract, guarding a paranoid tech executive in Lisbon, and learn the rules of their life: go-bag by the door, three identities, no attachments. A routine handoff goes wrong when Hazel spots surveillance that isn't theirs. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ilya Marchetti's POV. In a safehouse in Tallinn, whistleblower Ilya records a message that will only unlock if his voice matches — a dead-man's key to a server he helped build. He sends it into the dark, knowing it may kill whoever receives it. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as resolve.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A fixer named Odile offers Hazel a job protecting Ilya — triple rate, no questions, payment in untraceable crypto. Hazel takes it against instinct because the money buys a way out of the life entirely. Emotional beat: greed as self-deception.

chapters.title: Tallinn Arrival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reaches Tallinn to find Ilya already spooked, the safehouse wired with someone else's bugs. Their first meeting is hostile — Ilya assumes every contractor is a leash. Emotional beat: two professionals measuring each other for knives.

chapters.title: What the Server Holds
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya explains the network: autonomous targeting software trained on stolen biometric and behavioral data, sold to three governments under deniable contracts. The server in a decommissioned border station holds the training corpus — and his voiceprint is the only key. Emotional beat: confession as burden-sharing.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An extraction team hits the safehouse; Hazel and Ilya escape through the old town's medieval alleys, leaving one attacker alive on purpose. Hazel realizes the hunters knew the layout — someone inside the agency sold them out. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile pulls together the ragged team: disgraced signals analyst Priya, ex-military driver Tomas, and forger Wren, each carrying a grudge against the same agency. Found family begins forming around a kitchen table of stolen laptops. Emotional beat: wary belonging.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traces the network's financial spine and finds the training run was funded through a shell tied to Hazel's own former employer. She hesitates before telling Hazel. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by truth.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The team moves overland toward the border station, dodging a dragnet built from the very surveillance tools they're trying to destroy. Ilya freezes at a checkpoint and Hazel covers for him at real cost. Emotional beat: protection becoming devotion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Nights
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Stalled in a farmhouse, Ilya and Hazel trade histories over bad wine — Hazel's burned past, Ilya's complicity in building the thing he now fears. Something tender and unspoken takes root. Emotional beat: love arriving without permission.

chapters.title: The Agency Calls
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel's old handler, Marlowe, makes contact: stand down and be paid, or be listed. He offers Hazel reinstatement — the clean life back — in exchange for delivering Ilya. Emotional beat: duty and desire pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Wren's Forgeries
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren builds the team new identities for the final approach and quietly notices Hazel's documents keep getting revised — Hazel keeps almost erasing themselves. Emotional beat: seeing someone clearly before they see themselves.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Depot
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A supply run turns into a firefight; Tomas is wounded covering the retreat, and the team loses their vehicle cache. The enemy knows their route exactly — there's a second leak. Emotional beat: paranoia corroding trust.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya proves the leak is Odile, who has been feeding the agency to protect her brother held overseas. Confronted, Odile breaks down; the team must decide whether to use her or cut her loose. Emotional beat: mercy as a tactical choice.

chapters.title: Double Feed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Instead of punishing Odile, Hazel feeds her false plans to Marlowe — turning the leak into a weapon. The team preps the real assault under cover of the fake one. Emotional beat: rage refined into strategy.

chapters.title: Marlowe's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Marlowe corners Ilya alone and offers him the same deal: walk away, let the network live, be rich and safe. Ilya refuses, but Marlowe plants a seed of doubt about whether Hazel would do the same. Emotional beat: doubt as the enemy's sharpest tool.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The team moves on the border station during a storm, using Odile's misdirection to slip past the outer perimeter. Inside, they find the server hall guarded not by soldiers but by automated defenses running the network itself. Emotional beat: awe and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. At the server door, Ilya's voice unlocks the first layer — and triggers a failsafe that begins purging evidence and locking down the facility. To reach the core, someone must stay behind at the console manually. Emotional beat: sacrifice stepping forward voluntarily.

chapters.title: Burn It Down
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax. Hazel stays at the console while Ilya and the team fight their way out; Hazel faces Marlowe one last time among the racks, chooses Ilya and the crew over the badge, and initiates the thermite burn. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The network dies globally within hours; governments scramble to deny everything. Priya distributes the evidence to journalists, ensuring the burn wasn't in vain, while the team scatters to safehouses. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication.

chapters.title: Loose Threads
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren forges Hazel a final set of papers — this time with a name Hazel chose rather than inherited. Odile's brother is freed in the chaos; debts settle unevenly but honestly. Emotional beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: Cover and Border
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On a coast far from anywhere, Hazel meets Ilya and what remains of the crew. The go-bag sits unpacked by the door — not abandoned, just no longer packed out of fear. Hazel introduces themselves with their real name. Emotional beat: survival finally costing less than it bought.
